sections.title: Choose the right obligation structure
sections.content: Use tener que when a specific person has an obligation. Use hay que when the obligation is general.

sections.title: Compare the structures
rows: You have to work / It is necessary to work.

items.spanish: Tengo que llegar a las ocho.
items.english: I have to arrive at eight.
You have to arrive early. / It is necessary to arrive early.

sections.content: Ask whether the sentence names who has the obligation. If it does, use tener que. If it is a general rule, use hay que.
